input: It is worth noting that the adsorption of a dye from water onto a metal-organic framework was investigated in a series of batch tests carried out at 298 K. In each test, a known mass of the adsorbent was brought into contact with the dye solution, and the uptake was determined from the change in the solution concentration over the contact period. The equilibrium data were fitted using the Langmuir isotherm model, and the fitted capacity at pH 5 was found to be 136 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent. It should be emphasised that this capacity is the fitted Langmuir parameter, representing the dye loading that the fit assigns to the adsorbent as the equilibrium concentration increases, expressed on a per-gram basis. When an adsorbent dose of 0.6 g L-1 was used with an initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, the removal after 120 min reached 87%, which corresponds to a removed concentration of 43.5 mg L-1 and a residual concentration of 6.5 mg L-1. Importantly, the removal is expressed relative to the initial concentration, and the 87% figure is a removal fraction under the stated dose and contact time rather than a capacity. Furthermore, the dose and the contact time together define the conditions attached to the removal figure, so a different dose or a shorter contact time would be expected to give a different removal under the same test arrangement. Finally, the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured, which means that the fitted capacity of 136 mg per gram is established at pH 5 and cannot be assumed to apply at any other pH.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in batch tests at 298 K. Each test contacted a known mass of adsorbent with the dye solution, and uptake was obtained from the change in solution concentration over the contact period. Equilibrium data were fitted with the Langmuir isotherm, and the fitted capacity at pH 5 was 136 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent. Capacity here is the fitted Langmuir parameter: the dye loading the fit assigns to the adsorbent as the equilibrium concentration rises, stated per gram of adsorbent. At an adsorbent dose of 0.6 g L-1 and an initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, removal after 120 min was 87%, corresponding to a removed concentration of 43.5 mg L-1 and a residual concentration of 6.5 mg L-1. In a batch test the adsorbent and the solution are brought together once and left in contact, so the measured uptake belongs to the starting concentration and the contact period of the test rather than to a flowing stream. Removal is stated against the initial concentration, and the 87% figure is a removal fraction at the stated dose and contact time, not a capacity. The dose and the contact time fix the conditions of the removal figure; a different dose or a shorter contact time gives a different removal under the same test arrangement. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured, and the fitted capacity of 136 mg per gram is established at pH 5 and at no other pH. A capacity quoted for this adsorbent without its pH is incomplete, because the fit behind the figure was made at one pH only.
